title: Put the structure in the model: valid inertia, valid rates, graphs, and what a sensor can see
summary: A robot arm makes state and rate concrete, and four diagram slides say what a model can be forced to respect: a positive-definite mass matrix, domain constraints for mechanics and chemistry, a graph of who interacts, and a sensor map that hides part of the state.

read_the_figure.question: What does the model guarantee by construction, and what does the sensor let us recover?
read_the_figure.axes: Robot arm chart: horizontal and vertical position in illustrative units; each polyline is the arm in one pose (origin, elbow, tip). Diagram slides: boxes from input to guarantee or representation; the caption states the claim.
look_at: Three poses of the same arm are three states of one system; a motion is a path through the poses. The state is the pair of joint angles; the picture is its image in the plane.
Link lengths read off the poses: about 1.0 for the first link and about 0.7 for the second, constant in every pose. A model that predicts positions must keep these lengths.
Slide 26: M = L L^T + epsilon I; epsilon above zero guarantees a positive-definite mass matrix; the caption says structure helps and accuracy still needs data.
Slide 27: mechanics (valid inertia), chemistry (valid rates), both (physical tests); good structure removes impossible behaviour without inventing physics.
Slide 28: species graph (reaction graph) and atoms (molecular graph) are different representations; connectivity guides the model but does not determine rates.
Slide 29: hidden state, sensor map, measurement; a measurement may hide much of the state.
read_the_figure.proves: Structure removes whole classes of impossible predictions: negative kinetic energy, negative rates, links that stretch. It does not make the remaining predictions accurate. A sensor map decides which parts of the state can be inferred at all.
if_wrong: Link lengths that change between poses: the model violates the geometry it is supposed to preserve.
A mass matrix with a zero or negative eigenvalue: kinetic energy can vanish or turn negative.
A graph with a missing edge: the model cannot represent that interaction.
A sensor map with a null space: different states give the same measurement, so the state cannot be recovered.
must_check: That constraints are enforced by construction, not only encouraged by a penalty.
That a positive-definiteness test (smallest eigenvalue) is shown.
That the graph used for the model is stated and who its nodes are.
That the measurement map's rank is compared with the state dimension.

terms.meaning: The symmetric matrix that turns generalized velocities into kinetic energy.
A symmetric matrix with all eigenvalues above zero; every nonzero vector has positive energy.
A lower-triangular L; L L^T is automatically symmetric and non-negative definite.
Nodes are species, edges are reactions linking them.
The function from the hidden state to what a sensor reports.

remember: L L^T plus epsilon I is positive definite for any L when epsilon is above zero.
Kinetic energy 1/2 q-dot^T M q-dot is positive only if M is positive definite.
Rates of elementary reactions are positive by construction (Arrhenius form).
A graph encodes which variables may interact, not how strongly.
A measurement cannot separate states that differ only in its null space.

steps.title: Why L L^T + epsilon I is positive definite
steps.tex: x^{\mathsf T}(LL^{\mathsf T}+\varepsilon I)x=\lVert L^{\mathsf T}x\rVert^{2}+\varepsilon\lVert x\rVert^{2}\ \ge\ \varepsilon\lVert x\rVert^{2}>0
steps.note: The first term is a squared norm, so it is never negative; the second is strictly positive. The smallest eigenvalue is at least epsilon, whatever the network outputs for L.

steps.title: Forward kinematics of a two-link arm
steps.note: With lengths about 1.0 and 0.7 (read off the chart) the tip stays within distance 0.3 to 1.7 of the origin in every pose. This is a constraint a predictor of positions must obey.

steps.title: Positive rates by construction
steps.note: An Arrhenius form with a positive prefactor cannot return a negative rate; a free network output can. This is the 'valid rates' box of slide 27.

steps.title: Message passing on a graph
steps.note: Each node updates from its neighbours only. Which edges exist (the graph) is the structural choice of slide 28; the weights W and U are still learned.

steps.title: When a sensor hides the state
steps.note: The slide 29 statement in one line: the null space of the observation map is the part of the state a camera cannot see.

worked.title: A mass matrix that would otherwise be singular
worked.problem: Let L = [[1, 0], [0, 0]] and epsilon = 0.01. Find the eigenvalues of M = L L^T + epsilon I.

solution.text: L L^T is diag(1, 0), so M is diagonal.

worked.answer: 1.01 and 0.01, both positive; without epsilon the second would be zero and motion in that direction would cost no energy.

analyze.q: The three poses have the same link lengths. What would a model that predicts tip positions directly have to learn to respect that?
Why is epsilon in M = L L^T + epsilon I a design choice and not a detail?

evaluate.q: Slide 28 says connectivity guides the model but does not determine rates. What would you add to the figure to show that?
A camera sees positions but not velocities. What does the slide 29 caption imply for training a rate model from camera data?

create: Draw a fourth pose of the arm on the chart consistent with the two link lengths and write its joint angles.
Design a test panel for slide 27 that shows both a mechanics check and a chemistry check for one learned model.

checks.q: What does epsilon do in the mass matrix?
checks.answer: It guarantees all eigenvalues are at least epsilon, so M is positive definite.

checks.q: A rank-1 observation matrix on a 3-dimensional state. Dimension of the invisible part?
Why do structural constraints not guarantee accuracy?
checks.answer: They remove impossible predictions but leave the possible ones free: a valid mass matrix can still be wrong in value.

checks.q: A penalty term pushes rates to be positive. Is that equivalent to the Arrhenius form?
checks.answer: No: a penalty can be violated on unseen inputs; a form that is positive by construction cannot.

checks.q: Name a measurement map for the arm that makes the full state recoverable and one that does not.
checks.answer: Both joint angles recoverable; only the tip height is not (different angle pairs give the same height).
